question: In the already fitted E89 joint L2=.001 heads, which deployed score component carries fit gains and cross-family gains or losses?
method: Reuse the three original family folds, saved fit supports, RMS scales and head checkpoints. In memory only, set either both contextual vectors or both option-ID bias vectors to zero. Keep parent-choice bonus 1, unsupported-offer fallback, argmax ties and all source labels fixed. No refitting, weight rescaling or additional grid. The full model must reproduce every original out-of-fold choice and all E95 fit/fold summaries; zeroing both components must reproduce parent actions. Independently decode every selected terminal leaf from unpaced trees.
reason_for_fixed_checkpoint_set: One historical joint configuration, L2=.001 matching the fixed current E128 recipe. Its earlier results are exposed, so this is a post hoc explanatory diagnostic and is not model selection or new acceptance.
limits: Both score components were trained together. Removing one without refitting measures dependence of these fitted policies, not the achievable quality of a separately trained static or contextual model. Contextual frozen embeddings also contain candidate identity; context_only is not identity-free. E89 uses the historical engine, not current E121. Each family appears twice in fit evaluations and once out of fold; 3072 pooled fit rows are dependent. These historically exposed fit-fold results are not unseen acceptance. No current E128 labels, external label holdout or development outcomes are evaluated. No candidate adoption, training-job launch or E128/E131 gate change follows from these diagnostic comparisons.
